clue.text: Break down everything that's sprung up in wood

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for wood

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, sprung up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: Someone describes a plant that has shot up in woodland and lists it as everything that broke down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sprung up' reads the word upwards, giving LLA; 'that's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To break down is to give way or fall apart, synonyms for a structure or person failing.

clue.text: The French slip up and speak angrily

parts.note: le is French for the
a slip-up is a trip, a stumble

explanation.surface: A French speaker stumbles and then rants about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for giving full vent to anger, sounding off loudly.

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England

explanation.surface: Someone is rude while out on a canal or river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the stretch of sea separating the Isle of Wight from Hampshire on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolence is rude, contemptuous behaviour, so being insolent is showing disrespect.

clue.text: Half a dozen learned one's facial features

parts.note: half a dozen is six, VI in Roman numerals
a sage is a wise, learned person

explanation.surface: A scholar studies six distinctive features of someone's face.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a literary word for the face and its features or expression.

indicators.note: around says the word for hang is placed round the letter for old

parts.note: to hang in the air is to hover

explanation.surface: An instruction to loiter near an elderly former head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Hoover was the 31st President of the United States, serving from 1929 to 1933.

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it
T. S. Eliot's initials are TS

explanation.surface: An instruction to collect the poet's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot is the poet T. S. Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a standard pack of playing cards.

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of singes are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily scorches a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock formed under heat and pressure.

indicators.note: holding says the word for relish keeps the party letter within it

parts.note: relish, a zest or flavouring, is spice
L stands for Liberal, a political party

explanation.surface: A wedding planner enjoys a party at the reception.
explanation.definitionFit: To get spliced is informal slang for getting wed, from joining rope ends together.

clue.text: Burglar's not dangerous, given a wave

parts.note: something not dangerous is safe
a breaker is a large wave crashing on the shore

explanation.surface: A burglar is harmless, being offered a friendly wave.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thief who forces open strongboxes, a specialist kind of burglar.

indicators.note: shuffle means the letters of Harlem are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Names the writer of a dance tune, 'Harlem Shuffle' being a real 1960s song title.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was an Austrian composer of late-Romantic symphonies.

clue.text: Mayor prepared to embrace everyone with a lack of conscience

indicators.note: to embrace means the rearranged letters wrap around the word for everyone
prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters of Mayor are rearranged

parts.note: everyone is all

explanation.surface: A mayor gets ready to hug all the townsfolk, without scruples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' gives AMORY; the definition is the long phrase at the end, read adverbially.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting this way means behaving without regard to right or wrong, devoid of moral sense.

indicators.note: first says just the opening letter of Somerset is taken

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricket captain removes Somerset's leading spin bowler from the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner in cricket is a slow bowler; here it is a spinning top. Somerset is an English county with a cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off a service or show is to discontinue it, to halt it.

parts.note: a copper is a penny, abbreviated P
a testimonial or character statement is a reference

explanation.surface: A police officer's written character statement is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but here it is a penny coin, P in British money.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference is the option one favours, a chosen selection over others.

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters of considerate are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Remarks oddly that someone is thoughtful towards church vandals.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the violation of something sacred, such as damaging a holy place.

parts.note: EC is the abbreviation for the European Commission
static means unchanging, not moving

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that the Brussels bureaucracy is staying the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwhelmed with joy: an intense synonym for very pleased.

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the word for work above the next part

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
someone would-be is posing as something they are not

explanation.surface: A task is passed to someone hoping to become a foe.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally for a hostile side, as in the rival army facing one's own.

indicators.note: translation means turning something into another form, so the letters of Latin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A language exam requires turning English into Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: To necessitate or involve something as a consequence is a synonym for requiring it.

clue.text: Draw back from phone in church

indicators.note: in says the word for phone goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a mobile going off during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back or flinch, recoiling in fear or embarrassment.

clue.text: In a short time a prisoner becomes disloyal

indicators.note: In at the start signals the convict word goes inside the word for a short time

parts.note: an instant is a very short time
a con, short for convict, is a prisoner

explanation.surface: Someone jailed turns traitor within moments.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In' looks like letters for the answer's start, but it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fickle or unfaithful, not steady in loyalty or affection.

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A monarch issues a command to a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Highwayman has power in Italian city

indicators.note: in says the power letter sits inside the city name

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A robber holds sway in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick of that surname was an 18th-century English robber famed on the roads.

parts.note: par is the usual or normal level, as in par for the course

explanation.surface: It's the normal hour for leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate from someone is to take one's leave of them.

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
a rate is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: Someone trims the price of a material.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear or gash flesh, a wound made by slicing.

explanation.surface: Organising a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both ascending and an insurrection, two senses of going up.

clue.text: Pay a visit for game of cards with the family

parts.note: loo is an old card game
kin are one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Visiting relatives for an evening of card-playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is a historic trick-taking card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for making a brief call at someone's home.

clue.text: Apron for local tucking into tart

indicators.note: tucking into means placing the pub word inside the pastry word

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie
a local is one's neighbourhood pub, here an inn

explanation.surface: Someone wears a protective garment while eating a pastry at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' reads as eating, but it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British word for a pinafore, a protective garment.
